text: A catastrophic magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck near $\textbf{Port-au-Prince}$, the capital of $\textbf{Haiti}$, in January 2010, causing massive devastation.
explanation: The epicenter was just 25 km from the capital, leading to an estimated death toll of over 200,000 people.

text: The $\textbf{Deepwater Horizon}$ oil spill occurred in the $\textbf{Gulf of Mexico}$, becoming the largest marine oil spill in history.
explanation: The explosion on the BP-operated rig released millions of barrels of oil, impacting the coastlines of Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, and Florida.

text: The eruption of the volcano $\textbf{Eyjafjallajökull}$ in $\textbf{Iceland}$ grounded air traffic across Europe for weeks due to a massive $\textbf{Ash Cloud}$.
explanation: The ash plume entered the jet stream, forcing the closure of airspace over much of northern and western Europe.

text: The $\textbf{Burj Khalifa}$, the world's tallest building, officially opened in January 2010 in $\textbf{Dubai}$, United Arab Emirates.
explanation: Standing at 828 meters (2,717 ft), it surpassed Taipei 101 as the tallest structure in the world.

text: The $\textbf{2010 FIFA World Cup}$ was held in $\textbf{South Africa}$, marking the first time the tournament was hosted on the $\textbf{African}$ continent.
explanation: The event showcased cities like Johannesburg, Cape Town, and Durban to a global audience.

text: Thirty-three miners were trapped for 69 days in the $\textbf{San José Mine}$ located in the $\textbf{Atacama Desert}$ of $\textbf{Chile}$.
explanation: The dramatic rescue operation in the Copiapó region was watched by millions worldwide.

text: The $\textbf{2010 Winter Olympics}$ were hosted by $\textbf{Vancouver}$ in the province of $\textbf{British Columbia}$, Canada.
explanation: Events were held in Vancouver and the nearby resort town of Whistler.

text: A massive magnitude 8.8 earthquake struck off the coast of the $\textbf{Maule}$ region in $\textbf{Chile}$ in February 2010, triggering a tsunami.
explanation: It was one of the strongest earthquakes ever recorded, moving the city of Concepción more than 3 meters to the west.

text: Devastating floods submerged one-fifth of $\textbf{Pakistan}$ in 2010, caused by unprecedented $\textbf{Monsoon}$ rains swelling the $\textbf{Indus River}$.
explanation: The floods affected an estimated 20 million people and destroyed infrastructure across the country.

text: In 2010, $\textbf{China}$ officially overtook $\textbf{Japan}$ to become the world's second-largest $\textbf{Economy}$ by GDP.
explanation: This marked a major shift in global economic geography, with China trailing only the United States.

text: Mount $\textbf{Merapi}$, located on the densely populated island of $\textbf{Java}$ in $\textbf{Indonesia}$, erupted violently in late 2010.
explanation: The eruption forced the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of people in the Yogyakarta region.

text: Severe $\textbf{Wildfires}$ and a record heatwave struck western $\textbf{Russia}$ in 2010, threatening the capital city of $\textbf{Moscow}$ with heavy smog.
explanation: The heatwave destroyed a significant portion of Russia's grain crop and raised global wheat prices.

text: The $\textbf{Shanghai Expo 2010}$, the largest World's Fair in history, was held in $\textbf{China}$ on the banks of the $\textbf{Huangpu River}$.
explanation: More than 73 million people visited the expo, breaking previous attendance records.

text: The $\textbf{Netherlands Antilles}$ was dissolved in 2010, causing $\textbf{Curaçao}$ and $\textbf{Sint Maarten}$ to become constituent countries within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
explanation: This changed the political map of the Caribbean, giving these islands greater autonomy.

text: A massive toxic red sludge spill occurred in $\textbf{Hungary}$ in 2010, reaching the $\textbf{Danube River}$ and causing an ecological disaster.
explanation: The sludge escaped from an alumina plant reservoir in Ajka, burying nearby villages.

text: A giant $\textbf{Sinkhole}$ opened up in the middle of $\textbf{Guatemala City}$ in 2010, triggered by Tropical Storm Agatha.
explanation: The almost perfectly circular hole was caused by piping features and a burst sewer pipe.

text: The first of the $\textbf{Canterbury Earthquakes}$ struck near $\textbf{Christchurch}$, $\textbf{New Zealand}$ in September 2010, causing widespread damage.
explanation: While there were no fatalities in the 2010 quake, it weakened infrastructure leading to the deadly 2011 event.

text: The $\textbf{Three Gorges Dam}$ in $\textbf{China}$ reached its maximum water level capacity in 2010, marking a milestone for the world's largest power station.
explanation: The dam spans the Yangtze River and is a massive hydroelectric engineering project.

text: The $\textbf{Amazon Rainforest}$ experienced a severe $\textbf{Drought}$ in 2010, causing river levels to drop to historic lows in $\textbf{Brazil}$.
explanation: The drought affected transportation, fishing, and released huge amounts of carbon dioxide.

text: The $\textbf{Deepest Volcanic Vents}$ ever discovered were found in the $\textbf{Cayman Trough}$ in the Caribbean Sea in 2010.
explanation: Located 5,000 meters down, these vents host unique copper-rich ecosystems.

text: The $\textbf{Senkaku Islands}$ collision incident in 2010 heightened territorial tensions between $\textbf{China}$ and $\textbf{Japan}$ in the East China Sea.
explanation: A Chinese trawler collided with Japanese Coast Guard patrol boats near the disputed islands.

text: The $\textbf{Mentawai Islands}$ in $\textbf{Indonesia}$ were struck by a tsunami in 2010, following a magnitude 7.7 earthquake.
explanation: The islands are located off the western coast of Sumatra.

text: The $\textbf{Gulf of Aden}$ saw a peak in $\textbf{Piracy}$ activities in 2010, threatening one of the world's busiest shipping lanes off the coast of $\textbf{Somalia}$.
explanation: International naval task forces were deployed to protect vessels transiting toward the Suez Canal.

text: The $\textbf{2010 US Census}$ revealed that the center of population had shifted further to the $\textbf{South}$ and $\textbf{West}$.
explanation: States like Texas and Nevada saw significant growth, while the Rust Belt population stagnated.

text: Mount $\textbf{Sinabung}$ in $\textbf{Indonesia}$ erupted in 2010 after being dormant for over 400 years.
explanation: The volcano is located in the North Sumatra province.

text: The $\textbf{Yeonpyeong}$ shelling incident occurred in 2010, when $\textbf{North Korea}$ fired artillery at a $\textbf{South Korean}$ island near the maritime border.
explanation: This was one of the most serious escalations on the peninsula since the Korean War.

text: In 2010, $\textbf{Russia}$ and $\textbf{Norway}$ signed a treaty resolving a 40-year dispute over their maritime border in the $\textbf{Barents Sea}$.
explanation: The agreement opened up the region for potential oil and gas exploration.

text: The $\textbf{Shen Neng 1}$ coal carrier ran aground on the $\textbf{Great Barrier Reef}$ in 2010, damaging a large area of the World Heritage site.
explanation: The incident occurred off the coast of Queensland, Australia, leaving a toxic paint scar.

text: The $\textbf{International Court of Justice}$ ruled in 2010 that $\textbf{Kosovo}$'s declaration of independence from $\textbf{Serbia}$ did not violate international law.
explanation: Kosovo had unilaterally declared independence in 2008, a move contested by Serbia.

text: The $\textbf{Love Parade}$ disaster occurred in $\textbf{Duisburg}$, $\textbf{Germany}$, in 2010, leading to the permanent cancellation of the festival.
explanation: A stampede in a tunnel entrance caused the tragedy, shocking the nation.

text: Cyclone $\textbf{Giri}$ made landfall in $\textbf{Myanmar}$'s Rakhine State in 2010, causing significant damage just years after Cyclone Nargis.
explanation: The cyclone intensified rapidly in the Bay of Bengal before hitting the coast.

text: The $\textbf{Kampala}$ bombings in 2010 targeted crowds watching the World Cup final in $\textbf{Uganda}$.
explanation: The attacks were claimed by Al-Shabaab in retaliation for Uganda's support of the Somali government.

text: The $\textbf{Rio-Antirrio Bridge}$, an engineering marvel in $\textbf{Greece}$, was a symbol of infrastructure development despite the country's growing debt crisis in 2010.
explanation: It connects the Peloponnese peninsula with mainland Greece across the Gulf of Corinth.

text: In 2010, $\textbf{Qatar}$ was controversially awarded the hosting rights for the $\textbf{2022 FIFA World Cup}$, a decision that transformed the small peninsula's infrastructure.
explanation: Qatar became the first Middle Eastern nation selected to host the global tournament.

text: The $\textbf{Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant}$ in $\textbf{Iran}$ began fueling in 2010, marking the start of the country's nuclear energy program amid sanctions.
explanation: The plant is located on the Persian Gulf coast.

text: A Polish Air Force jet crashed near $\textbf{Smolensk}$, $\textbf{Russia}$ in 2010, killing the Polish President and many top officials.
explanation: The crash occurred in thick fog while the delegation was en route to a memorial service.

text: The $\textbf{Stuxnet}$ computer worm was discovered in 2010, specifically targeting nuclear facilities in $\textbf{Natanz}$, $\textbf{Iran}$.
explanation: It was the first known cyberweapon to cause physical damage to industrial infrastructure (centrifuges).

text: The $\textbf{Danube Delta}$ borders $\textbf{Romania}$ and $\textbf{Ukraine}$ and is the second largest river delta in Europe.
explanation: Most of the delta lies within Romania, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

text: The $\textbf{Spratly Islands}$ dispute intensified in 2010 as $\textbf{US}$ Secretary of State Hillary Clinton declared freedom of navigation in the $\textbf{South China Sea}$ a national interest.
explanation: This signaled greater US involvement in the territorial disputes of the region.

text: The $\textbf{One World Trade Center}$ in $\textbf{New York City}$ reached a construction milestone in 2010, surpassing the height of the $\textbf{Empire State Building}$.
explanation: It was part of the rebuilding of the World Trade Center complex following the 9/11 attacks.
